title: Greek Worlds
tagline: Poleis, Persia, a democracy of some of the men, a long war, and Alexander’s empire that did not stay one kingdom
summary: This course refuses the picture of a single Greek nation waiting to become Europe. It teaches the polis, the Persian wars as wars against a great empire, the exclusions inside Athenian democracy, the Peloponnesian War as a Greek war, and Alexander’s conquest as the start of several Hellenistic kingdoms.
overview: The Greek past that later Europeans claimed was a world of poleis: small citizen-states, colonies, and arguments about who the citizens were. Persia was the great power on the other side of the Aegean. A story that needs the Persians to be a formless East is not using the evidence.

Athenian democracy is real and it is narrow. The chapters name who voted, who did not, and which laws tightened the citizen body. Socrates’ death is a fact about that city, not a summary of the Greek mind.

The Peloponnesian War was fought among Greeks. It is not a rehearsal for a later clash of civilisations. Alexander’s campaign destroyed the Achaemenid imperial centre and did not leave a single successor. The Hellenistic kingdoms are the result, and they are the world Rome later met.
outcomes: Define a polis and say why it is not a nation-state.
Place Marathon, Salamis and Plataea, and describe Persia as an empire rather than as a symbol.
State who was excluded from the Athenian citizen body after the mid-fifth century.
Explain the Peloponnesian War as a war among Greek states, with dates for its start and for Athens’ surrender.
Explain why Alexander’s death in 323 BCE is the start of a political problem, not the completion of a Greek nation.

chapters.title: What a polis was
chapters.summary: A polis is a citizen community and a territory. Colonies, leagues and tyrannies belong in the picture. A Greek nation does not.

chapters.title: The Persian wars
chapters.summary: Marathon, Thermopylae, Salamis and Plataea, and the Achaemenid empire as a state with its own politics.

chapters.title: A democracy of some of the men
chapters.summary: Cleisthenes, the institutions, Pericles’ citizenship law, and the exclusion of women, enslaved people and metics.

chapters.title: A war among Greeks
chapters.summary: From 431 to 404 BCE: empire inside the Aegean, plague, Sicily, and the surrender of Athens. Philosophy is not the same thing as the city’s policy.

chapters.title: Alexander and after
chapters.summary: Macedon, Chaeronea, the campaign to Babylon, and the kingdoms that followed a death in 323 BCE.

history.title: Marathon
history.detail: A Persian expedition is defeated by Athens and its allies. The war is not over.

history.title: Salamis
history.detail: In the same campaign season as Thermopylae, a Greek fleet defeats the Persian fleet at Salamis.

history.title: The Peloponnesian War begins
history.detail: Athens and Sparta, and their allies, begin the war that ends with Athens’ surrender in 404 BCE.

history.title: Death of Alexander
history.detail: Alexander dies in Babylon. The conquered empire is divided among his commanders rather than inherited as one Greek state.

references.title: Greece in the Making, 1200–479 BC
references.note: A history of the archaic Greek world that does not start from a later national story.
